evaluations.question: Tell me about a time you had to design or operate a high-throughput transaction system where duplicate execution or data drift could cause severe financial loss.
evaluations.candidate_response: In ERP and fintech procurement, ledger drift and duplicate payments cost millions. Our objective was to guarantee 100% duplicate prevention under 50,000+ burst load. To solve this, I architected ApexFlow, a high-throughput 3-way reconciliation engine (PO vs GRN vs Invoice). I implemented a cryptographic SHA-256 idempotency ledger with SQLite WAL, a 3-state self-healing circuit breaker, and an async saga rollback DAG. Under stress testing, the engine clocked 56,179 records/second with p99 latency under 0.02 milliseconds and 0% duplicate leakage, verified across 15 automated test suites.

evaluations.question: How do you prevent circular event loop deadlocks and thread-safety race conditions in concurrent Python microservices?
evaluations.candidate_response: When scaling concurrent microservices, binding asyncio.Lock() at import time attaches it to whatever loop was active at import, causing fatal deadlocks when invoked from worker loops. Our objective was 100% thread safety across 50+ concurrent background tasks. I implemented lazy property lock initialization so locks bind exclusively inside active running coroutines. Furthermore, for in-memory telemetry registries accessed across threads, I upgraded non-reentrant threading.Lock to threading.RLock, allowing re-entrant inspection without self-deadlock. This delivered 0 deadlocks across 114 test suites and sustained 56,000 ops/sec.

keyword_alignment.feedback: Matched 6/6 target technical concepts (lock, asyncio, lazy, rlock, thread, deadlock)

evaluations.question: Autonomous AI agents frequently get stuck in infinite retry loops and burn thousands of dollars in tokens. How did you solve this?
evaluations.candidate_response: Unconstrained agent loops suffer from cyclic hallucination and runaway token spend. Our task was to enforce hard cost bounds and zero repetitive errors. I built the ApexAgentic Task Runtime with three deterministic layers: first, a sliding-window Token & Cost Governor with strict 100,000 token budget caps; second, an Epistemic Failed Solution Memory that computes SHA-256 signatures of failed attempts and intercepts repeated dead-ends before calling the LLM; and third, a cryptographically signed HITL approval gate for destructive tool invocations. This eliminated 100% of cyclic loops and reduced redundant token spend by 50% across 4 automated test suites.

keyword_alignment.feedback: Matched 5/6 target technical concepts (apexagentic, failed solution memory, sha-256, hitl, cost)
